offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 23rd of 32.
offence.blurb: No team put the ball in the air more often, and with Kyler Murray now in Minnesota it is Jacoby Brissett throwing it, mostly to tight end Trey McBride and Marvin Harrison Jr. Plenty of passing touchdowns, very little coming from the run.

defence.note: Among the worst in the league for points allowed last season — 29th of 32.
defence.blurb: A unit that rarely gets to the quarterback despite Josh Sweat leading the rush, leaning instead on a young cornerback pairing of Will Johnson and Denzel Burke.

specialTeams.note: Among the worst in the league at kicking field goals last season — 30th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Chad Ryland has been reliable on field goals, but that is about the only part of this group that stands out, with Devin Duvernay handling returns.

offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 24th of 32.
offence.blurb: One of the more run-leaning offences in the league, built around Bijan Robinson, with Tua Tagovailoa throwing to Drake London. Touchdowns through the air have been hard to come by.

defence.note: Middle of the league for points allowed last season, 19th of 32.
defence.blurb: A group that gets after the quarterback as well as almost anyone and forces its share of turnovers, with A.J. Terrell Jr. the anchor in the secondary.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 24th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Veteran kicker Nick Folk has been steady enough, and Zachariah Branch returns kicks; otherwise there is little here that stands out.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 11th of 32.
offence.blurb: The most run-leaning offence in the league, and the most effective per carry, with Derrick Henry carrying the load and Lamar Jackson himself a big part of the running game.

defence.note: Middle of the league for points allowed last season, 18th of 32.
defence.blurb: A veteran-heavy front with Nnamdi Madubuike and Calais Campbell that has struggled to generate sacks, so much of the work falls on corners Nate Wiggins and Marlon Humphrey.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 12th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: An unremarkable group, with Tyler Loop dependable on field goals and no real weapon in the return game.

offence.note: Among the best in the league for points scored last season — 4th of 32.
offence.blurb: Leans on the run more than most and scored more rushing touchdowns than any team, largely because Josh Allen carries the ball himself well over a hundred times a year alongside James Cook III.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 12th of 32.
defence.blurb: A middling unit that neither pressures the quarterback much nor takes the ball away often, with Christian Benford and Maxwell Hairston at cornerback.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 8th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Tyler Bass has been among the most accurate kickers in the league, which is the clearest strength of an otherwise ordinary group.

offence.note: Among the worst in the league for points scored last season — 27th of 32.
offence.blurb: A slightly run-leaning offence under Dave Canales that struggles to gain much through the air, with Bryce Young himself a regular runner and Chuba Hubbard carrying the load on the ground.

defence.note: Middle of the league for points allowed last season, 15th of 32.
defence.blurb: A defence built on its interior line, Derrick Brown and Tershawn Wharton, that rarely gets to the quarterback but takes the ball away at a decent clip, helped by corners Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 22nd of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Little to it beyond a reliable kicker in Ryan Fitzgerald; the rest of the return and coverage work is unremarkable.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 9th of 32.
offence.blurb: Ben Johnson's offence runs the ball well and hardly ever gives it away — fewer turnovers than any other team — with Caleb Williams adding plenty of carries himself alongside D'Andre Swift.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 23rd of 32.
defence.blurb: A defence that lives on taking the ball away, more than anyone else, while getting little pressure on the quarterback outside of Montez Sweat and Dayo Odeyingbo.

specialTeams.note: Middle of the league at kicking field goals last season, 18th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Cairo Santos is dependable on field goals; nothing else here stands out either way.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 12th of 32.
offence.blurb: One of the most pass-happy offences in the league, throwing on nearly two of every three plays with Joe Burrow feeding Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, and very little coming from the run.

defence.note: Among the worst in the league for points allowed last season — 30th of 32.
defence.blurb: A young, thin defence that neither pressures the quarterback much nor holds up behind it, with Boye Mafe the main name up front and Dax Hill and DJ Turner II in the secondary.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 9th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Anchored by Evan McPherson's accurate kicking, with Charlie Jones handling returns.

offence.note: Among the worst in the league for points scored last season — 31st of 32.
offence.blurb: Cleveland throws a bit more than most teams but gets less from it than anyone, and coughs the ball up often; rookie back Quinshon Judkins is the piece most worth watching.

defence.note: Middle of the league for points allowed last season, 14th of 32.
defence.blurb: A pass-rushing defence, now led by Jared Verse and Alex Wright after Myles Garrett was traded to the Rams for picks, though it doesn't force many turnovers.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 10th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Andre Szmyt has been accurate on field goals, and the unit does its job without drawing attention.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 7th of 32.
offence.blurb: A passing offence first, throwing a bit more often than most teams, with Dak Prescott spreading it to CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Jake Ferguson. Javonte Williams and the run game go at a decent clip without being the point.

defence.note: Among the worst in the league for points allowed last season — 32nd of 32.
defence.blurb: A unit that rarely takes the ball away and doesn't get to the quarterback much, leaning on big interior linemen in Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark. Veteran pass rusher Von Miller has just been added on a cheap one-year deal.

specialTeams.note: Middle of the league at kicking field goals last season, 16th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Built around two specialists: Brandon Aubrey, who is one of the surest field goal kickers in the league, and returner KaVontae Turpin. Everything else about it is ordinary.

offence.note: Middle of the league for points scored last season, 14th of 32.
offence.blurb: They throw more than almost anyone, but the passes are short and don't gain much — only a handful of teams get less per throw. Bo Nix is also a real part of the running game, carrying the ball himself often.

defence.note: Among the best in the league for points allowed last season — 3rd of 32.
defence.blurb: A pass-rushing unit above all, sacking the quarterback more than any other team through Nik Bonitto and Zach Allen, with Pat Surtain II covering behind them. It just doesn't force many turnovers.

specialTeams.note: Middle of the league at kicking field goals last season, 14th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Wil Lutz is among the most accurate kickers in the league and Marvin Mims Jr. handles returns; beyond that it's a middling group.

offence.note: Among the best in the league for points scored last season — 5th of 32.
offence.blurb: A balanced attack that does everything well — Jared Goff throwing to Amon-Ra St. Brown and Sam LaPorta, Jahmyr Gibbs running behind Penei Sewell. It does give the ball away a fair bit.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 22nd of 32.
defence.blurb: A group that gets after the quarterback well, with Aidan Hutchinson the centre of it, but doesn't force many turnovers. Cornerback Terrion Arnold has just left for Seattle, thinning an already young back end.

specialTeams.note: Among the worst in the league at kicking field goals last season — 27th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Jake Bates is reliable enough on field goals, but there's little else here — the return and coverage work drags the whole unit down.

offence.note: Middle of the league for points scored last season, 16th of 32.
offence.blurb: One of the most run-leaning offences in the league, handing off to Josh Jacobs even though the ground game grinds rather than gashes. When Jordan Love does throw it's very productive, and they almost never give the ball away.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 11th of 32.
defence.blurb: A solid, unspectacular unit that neither sacks the quarterback often nor forces many turnovers. The big change is Micah Parsons arriving to rush the passer alongside an already sturdy interior.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 23rd of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: A weak unit overall, though the kicking itself has been fairly accurate. Trey Smack handles the kicks and Skyy Moore the returns.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 13th of 32.
offence.blurb: Balanced in how often they throw, and it all leans on C.J. Stroud and Nico Collins, because the running game gains very little per carry. Their saving grace is how rarely they hand the ball over.

defence.note: Among the best in the league for points allowed last season — 2nd of 32.
defence.blurb: A defence that hunts the ball, with Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter pressuring the quarterback and Derek Stingley Jr. cleaning up behind them. Takeaways come often.

specialTeams.note: Among the best in the league at kicking field goals last season — 6th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Built around a reliable kicker in Ka'imi Fairbairn, who makes almost everything he attempts, with Jaylin Noel handling returns.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 8th of 32.
offence.blurb: Nothing unusual in how often they throw, but they score on the ground about as well as anyone, with Jonathan Taylor carrying the load and rookie tight end Tyler Warren helping Daniel Jones.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 21st of 32.
defence.blurb: A middling group without an obvious strength up front, though the two corners, Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward, are the names to know.

specialTeams.note: Among the best in the league at kicking field goals last season — 2nd of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Blake Grupe makes nearly all his kicks, which is the main reason this unit stands out.

offence.note: Among the best in the league for points scored last season — 6th of 32.
offence.blurb: Trevor Lawrence is a big part of the running game himself, carrying the ball far more than most quarterbacks, while Brian Thomas Jr. is the main target. Handoffs to the backs gain little.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 8th of 32.
defence.blurb: A defence that takes the ball away as often as almost any team, even though Travon Walker and Josh Hines-Allen don't get to the quarterback much. Travis Hunter plays here as well as on offence.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 13th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Cam Little is a dependable kicker and Bhayshul Tuten doubles up as the return man; otherwise an ordinary unit.

offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 21st of 32.
offence.blurb: One of the most pass-heavy attacks in the league, with Patrick Mahomes throwing to Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy and Travis Kelce, though the yards per throw are modest. Mahomes runs a fair bit himself.

defence.note: Among the best in the league for points allowed last season — 6th of 32.
defence.blurb: A defence that keeps points down without much help from sacks or takeaways, and it just lost its best cornerback, Trent McDuffie, in a trade to the Rams.

specialTeams.note: Middle of the league at kicking field goals last season, 15th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Harrison Butker kicks accurately, but the rest of the unit is fairly ordinary.

offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 20th of 32.
offence.blurb: One of the more pass-heavy attacks in the league, run through Justin Herbert, who also carries the ball himself a fair amount. Ladd McConkey is the main target; the running game rarely finishes drives.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 9th of 32.
defence.blurb: A defence that gets after the quarterback and takes the ball away, with Khalil Mack still the name up front and a young interior pairing beside him.

specialTeams.note: Among the best in the league at kicking field goals last season — 5th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Built around Cameron Dicker, who made his field goals more reliably than any other kicker, with Derius Davis handling returns.

offence.note: Among the best in the league for points scored last season — 1st of 32.
offence.blurb: A balanced attack that throws about as often as anyone else but scores through the air more than any team, with Matthew Stafford spreading it between Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. Kyren Williams carries the ground work.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 10th of 32.
defence.blurb: A pass-rushing, ball-hawking group that just got two enormous additions: Myles Garrett up front and Trent McDuffie at cornerback, both arriving by trade.

specialTeams.note: Among the worst in the league at kicking field goals last season — 28th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Harrison Mevis has been dependable on field goals, but the wider return and coverage work drags this group down.

offence.note: Among the worst in the league for points scored last season — 32nd of 32.
offence.blurb: Throws more than most teams even though Kirk Cousins isn't getting much per attempt, and the running game behind Ashton Jeanty has gone nowhere. Brock Bowers is the most reliable weapon; new centre Tyler Linderbaum arrives on a record deal.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 25th of 32.
defence.blurb: A fairly anonymous group without a standout pass rusher or a takeaway habit, leaning on Kwity Paye up front and two young cornerbacks.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 25th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Matt Gay has been steady on field goals, but little else in the return and coverage game stands out.

offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 25th of 32.
offence.blurb: Runs the ball more than most teams and gets good yardage doing it through De'Von Achane, but gives the ball away a lot. Malik Willis is the new starter after Miami released Tua Tagovailoa at huge cost.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 24th of 32.
defence.blurb: A young, linebacker-led group built around Chop Robinson's pass rush, with inexperienced cornerbacks behind them and no real standout strength.

specialTeams.note: Among the best in the league at kicking field goals last season — 4th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Riley Patterson has been about as accurate on field goals as any kicker, and Malik Washington doubles up as the return man.

offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 26th of 32.
offence.blurb: An offence that gives the ball away more than anyone in the league and gets little through the air despite Justin Jefferson, and it now belongs to Kyler Murray after J.J. McCarthy was benched.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 7th of 32.
defence.blurb: Built on pressure — they get to the quarterback about as often as any defence — with Dallas Turner and the interior linemen leading the way and a fair number of takeaways behind it.

specialTeams.note: Among the best in the league at kicking field goals last season — 3rd of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Anchored by Will Reichard, who missed almost nothing from placekicks, the most reliable leg in the league.

offence.note: Among the best in the league for points scored last season — 2nd of 32.
offence.blurb: Gets more out of every throw than any other offence, and Drake Maye is a genuine part of the running game himself with over a hundred carries. A.J. Brown's arrival from Philadelphia gives him a true number one target.

defence.note: Among the best in the league for points allowed last season — 4th of 32.
defence.blurb: A defence that holds up without much pass rush or many takeaways, leaning instead on a strong cornerback pair in Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis III.

specialTeams.note: Middle of the league at kicking field goals last season, 19th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Andy Borregales is dependable on field goals; the rest of the unit is fairly ordinary.

offence.note: Among the worst in the league for points scored last season — 28th of 32.
offence.blurb: They throw more often than most teams, largely because the running game goes nowhere — almost no one gains less per carry. Tyler Shough is the young quarterback under new coach Kellen Moore.

defence.note: Middle of the league for points allowed last season, 16th of 32.
defence.blurb: A middling defence whose best trait is getting after the quarterback, with veterans Cameron Jordan and Chase Young up front.

specialTeams.note: Among the worst in the league at kicking field goals last season — 32nd of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Charlie Smyth misses too many kicks, and there is little here to make up for it.

offence.note: Middle of the league for points scored last season, 17th of 32.
offence.blurb: A young offence that scores plenty on the ground but rarely through the air, with Jaxson Dart carrying the ball himself a great deal alongside Cam Skattebo, under new coach John Harbaugh.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 26th of 32.
defence.blurb: A defence that hardly ever takes the ball away, though rookie Abdul Carter and a rebuilt cornerback group give it some pressure and cover.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 11th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Ben Sauls has been the most accurate placekicker in the league, which is the clearest thing this unit does well.

offence.note: Among the worst in the league for points scored last season — 29th of 32.
offence.blurb: They throw a bit less than most teams, and with good reason — the running game moves the ball fine while the passing game gains very little, with Breece Hall and Garrett Wilson the main sources of anything.

defence.note: Among the worst in the league for points allowed last season — 31st of 32.
defence.blurb: A defence that almost never takes the ball away and rarely gets to the quarterback, leaning on young pass rusher Will McDonald IV for what pressure there is.

specialTeams.note: Among the best in the league at kicking field goals last season — 1st of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Built on Jason Sanders, who missed almost nothing all year, with Kene Nwangwu handling kick returns.

offence.note: Middle of the league for points scored last season, 19th of 32.
offence.blurb: Run and pass in league-average proportion, but Jalen Hurts himself is a big part of the running game alongside Saquon Barkley. Trading A.J. Brown away leaves DeVonta Smith as the main receiver.

defence.note: Among the best in the league for points allowed last season — 5th of 32.
defence.blurb: A strong, balanced defence anchored inside by Jalen Carter, with a young cornerback pair in Quinyon Mitchell and Riq Woolen.

specialTeams.note: Among the worst in the league at kicking field goals last season — 31st of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Jake Elliott's kicking has held up better than the rest of the unit, which gets little going in the return game.

offence.note: Middle of the league for points scored last season, 15th of 32.
offence.blurb: They throw a little more than most, but the passes are short ones that don't gain much, with Aaron Rodgers feeding DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr.

defence.note: Middle of the league for points allowed last season, 17th of 32.
defence.blurb: An aggressive group that gets after the quarterback and forces plenty of turnovers, led by Alex Highsmith and veteran Cameron Heyward, even if the overall results are middling.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 20th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: An unremarkable unit without an obvious strength, with Chris Boswell handling the kicking.

offence.note: Among the best in the league for points scored last season — 3rd of 32.
offence.blurb: One of the least pass-heavy offences in the league, but the throws they do make go a long way, usually to Jaxon Smith-Njigba or Rashid Shaheed. The flip side is that they give the ball away often.

defence.note: Among the best in the league for points allowed last season — 1st of 32.
defence.blurb: A well-rounded defence that pressures and takes the ball away, built around cornerback Devon Witherspoon, who has just been signed to a long extension, with Terrion Arnold added cheaply behind him.

specialTeams.note: Middle of the league at kicking field goals last season, 17th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Jason Myers is reliable on field goals and Rashid Shaheed doubles up as the kick returner; nothing else stands out.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 10th of 32.
offence.blurb: Slightly more run-leaning than most teams, but the running lanes aren't there — the points come through Brock Purdy's arm to Kittle, Evans and Deebo Samuel, with McCaffrey catching as well as carrying.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 13th of 32.
defence.blurb: A young front that almost never gets to the quarterback and rarely forces a mistake; the corner pair of Lenoir and Green carries much of the load.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 7th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Built around a kicker, Eddy Pineiro, who missed almost nothing all year.

offence.note: Middle of the league for points scored last season, 18th of 32.
offence.blurb: Balanced in how often they throw, and modest on a per-play basis either way. Baker Mayfield tucks the ball and runs fairly often himself, with Bucky Irving handling the carries.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 20th of 32.
defence.blurb: A ball-hawking group that takes the ball away often, with a fairly ordinary pass rush; young corner Benjamin Morrison lines up opposite Zyon McCollum.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 21st of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Chase McLaughlin is dependable on field goals; there is little else here that stands out.

offence.note: Among the worst in the league for points scored last season — 30th of 32.
offence.blurb: Throws the ball about as often as any team in the league, with little to show for it — young quarterback Cam Ward is still finding his feet and is himself a fair chunk of the running game.

defence.note: Among the worst in the league for points allowed last season — 28th of 32.
defence.blurb: Robert Saleh's front, led by Franklin-Myers and Jermaine Johnson, gets after the quarterback reasonably well, but the group hardly ever comes away with the ball.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 26th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Nothing here jumps out, in kicking or in the return game with Chimere Dike.

offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 22nd of 32.
offence.blurb: One of the most run-leaning offences in the league, and Jayden Daniels' own carries are a big part of that; they move the ball on the ground but score through the air far less, and give it away too often.

defence.note: Among the worst in the league for points allowed last season — 27th of 32.
defence.blurb: They pressure the quarterback decently but almost never take the ball away, leaning on young corners Trey Amos and Mike Sainristil.

specialTeams.note: Among the worst in the league at kicking field goals last season — 29th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: A shaky unit with an inexperienced kicker in Drew Stevens and no real weapon in the return game.
